chunks: The Magians inherit through blood relations, and they do not inherit through invalid marriage. So if a Magian man dies and leaves behind his mother, and she is his sister and she is his wife, then the estate belongs to her on account of her being a mother; and she has nothing on account of her being a sister and that she is a wife.

key_terms.أُمٌّ: Mother, the qualifying relationship through which inheritance is recognized in this case.
key_terms.اَلْمَجُوسُ: The Magians, i.e. Zoroastrians, discussed here in the context of inheritance rulings.
key_terms.بِالنَّسَبِ: Through blood lineage or kinship relation.
key_terms.بِالنِّكَاحِ الْفَاسِدِ: Through an invalid or corrupt marriage bond, which does not establish inheritance here.
key_terms.زَوْجَةٌ: Wife, a marital status that does not establish inheritance here due to the invalid marriage.

ai.seo_question: Do Magians inherit through blood lineage or through invalid marriage in Shia inheritance law?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling regarding the inheritance of the Magians: inheritance is recognized through lineage, but not through a corrupt or invalid marriage. In the stated case, the woman inherits only through her status as mother, not through the prohibited marital bond nor through the sibling relation as treated in this ruling.
